title: Driver: car repairs NOT covered, even with extended warranty
summary: A news report on CarShield customers whose claims were denied, with the FTC warning that service contracts are not the same as warranties.

assertions.quote: warranties come with the car this is an added expense

verdicts.note: FTC and the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act distinguish a manufacturer warranty (included, from the maker) from a paid third-party service contract.
FTC's consumer guide treats an auto service contract/extended warranty as legally distinct from the factory warranty bundled with the vehicle, since it's bought separately as an optional add-on.

assertions.quote: they never held up their end of the bargain

verdicts.note: A real and widely reported pattern among complaint sites and lawsuits, but far from universal across all providers.
CR says automotive service plans sold by third-party companies rather than manufacturers have been a particular problem, with many customer complaints that providers refuse to pay claims.

assertions.quote: the BBB has received nearly 300 complaints on car shield

verdicts.note: Documented by consumer-protection groups tracking complaint volume against specific advertised providers.

assertions.quote: ask what's not included find out who performs or pays for repairs

verdicts.note: Standard FTC consumer guidance for this product category.
